text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS

-- Government plan for Credit Lyonnais to include sale of European branch network and three billion francs in state help, ahead of a gradual possible privatisation. Plan to be presented to European Commission today or tomorrow.
-- Public sector unions fear wage austerity after Prime Minister Lionel Jospin vowed to cut public deficit to three percent of GDP in 1998.
-- Some minority shareholders file complaint with Paris court against Lagardere over terms of a 1993 share issue.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Bill on job creation for the young includes plans for a new five-year contract, which may be extended to the private sector to increase labour market flexibility.
-- U.S. investor interested in bidding for Societe du Louvre.
-- Daily Le Monde chairman Jean-Marie Colombani in an interview confirms is interested in buying weekly l'Express.
L'AGEFI
-- Paris futures and options market Matif SA chairman Gerard Pfauwadel in an interview says Matif to concentrate on bond-related products.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- GAN chairman Didier Pfeiffer in an interview says privatisation to be implemented through private placement to insurance and banking sector partners, search for bidders to be launched very soon.

-- Former minister Michel Delebarre in charge of implementing a dialogue with France Telecom unions over a possible partial privatisation met with CGT and FO unions yesterday. Union sources said they expected the government to go ahead with a partial sale.
-- CDR company set up to sell off Credit Lyonnais assets may sell golf network Blue Green to a British bank.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- European commission seen unenthusiastic over possible bid for GAN by AGF, according to a report from the commission's competition board, quoted by Liberation.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- European commission approves a 23.76 billion francs bailout to insurer GAN, before a privatisation.
